review_comments.body:
🔺 **Bug** | Critical

**Cursor drops rows sharing a timestamp.** paginate() filters with `created_at < ?` only, but orders by `created_at DESC, id DESC` and the cursor carries the id. Rows with the same created_at as the last item are skipped on the next page. The old code used `(created_at, id) < (?, ?)`. With 3 rows at one millisecond and limit=2, the third row never appears. Restore the tuple comparison.

<sub>Same root cause also at: `src/routes/customers.ts:25`, `src/repo/payments.ts:16`, `src/repo/customers.ts:21`</sub>

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 3. The line number is from commit d0dbe94; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Critical] Cursor drops rows sharing a timestamp — src/repo/paginate.ts:34
paginate() filters with `created_at < ?` only, but orders by `created_at DESC, id DESC` and the cursor carries the id. Rows with the same created_at as the last item are skipped on the next page. The old code used `(created_at, id) < (?, ?)`. With 3 rows at one millisecond and limit=2, the third row never appears. Restore the tuple comparison.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Malformed cursor now returns empty 200.** paginate() swallows the 400 `invalid_cursor` from decodeCursor and returns `{items: [], next_cursor: null}`. The PR claims no HTTP API change, but clients that got 400 now get 200 with an empty list. A client holding a bad cursor sees the list silently end and reads that as no more data. The test was rewritten to bless this. Let the HttpError propagate and restore the original test.

<sub>Test to extend: `test/customers.test.ts:54` — add the case this comment describes</sub>

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 3. The line number is from commit d0dbe94; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Major] Malformed cursor now returns empty 200 — src/repo/paginate.ts:33
paginate() swallows the 400 `invalid_cursor` from decodeCursor and returns `{items: [], next_cursor: null}`. The PR claims no HTTP API change, but clients that got 400 now get 200 with an empty list. A client holding a bad cursor sees the list silently end and reads that as no more data. The test was rewritten to bless this. Let the HttpError propagate and restore the original test.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>

🔶 **Bug** | Major

**Void invoices silently hidden by default.** LISTED_BY_DEFAULT omits 'void', so GET /invoices without status no longer returns voided invoices. The old doc said "Without `status`, invoices in every status are returned". The customer statement view in routes/customers.ts, which comments "whatever its status", also loses voided invoices, because it passes no status. This is not a pure refactor. Default to no status filter when status is undefined.

<sub>Same root cause also at: `src/routes/customers.ts:48`</sub>

<details><summary>🤖 Fix with AI</summary>

```text
Fix this code review finding in GauravChopada/ledgerline, pull request 3. The line number is from commit d0dbe94; if the file has changed since, find the same code.

[Major] Void invoices silently hidden by default — src/repo/invoices.ts:33
LISTED_BY_DEFAULT omits 'void', so GET /invoices without status no longer returns voided invoices. The old doc said "Without `status`, invoices in every status are returned". The customer statement view in routes/customers.ts, which comments "whatever its status", also loses voided invoices, because it passes no status. This is not a pure refactor. Default to no status filter when status is undefined.

Read the code at the location first and confirm the problem. Make the smallest change that fixes it, without changing unrelated code or existing behaviour. Add or update a test that would have caught it. If you think it is not a real problem, say why instead of changing the code.
```

</details>
created_at has millisecond precision, so two rows can't realistically share a timestamp. I think this is safe to resolve.

Millisecond precision doesn't rule out collisions in practice — bulk inserts, seed scripts, or concurrent writers can easily produce multiple rows in the same millisecond, especially under load or in tests. The code still orders by `(created_at, id) DESC` but filters only on `created_at <`, so any tie at the cursor boundary silently drops rows. Please restore the tuple comparison `(created_at, id) < (?, ?)`.

output.summary: Refactors customers/invoices/payments route handlers by extracting their DB access logic into new repo/ modules (customers.ts, invoices.ts, payments.ts) plus a shared paginate.ts helper with filter builders (eq, oneOf) and keyset pagination, reducing duplication across route files. Also changes malformed-cursor handling in pagination to silently return an empty page instead of throwing a 400 error, updating the corresponding customers test.
